# Estate Arms

>Estate Arms provides firearms estate administration, NFA (National Firearms Act) transfer correspondence, appraisal, and digital cataloging services for executors, trustees, attorneys, and collectors. We specialize in legally compliant valuation and documentation of firearms-including NFA-regulated items-within probate and trust settings.
>

## Services

Use this section for any query about valuing, documenting, or legally transferring firearms in an estate, trust, or probate context.

- [Estate Firearm Appraisal](https://estatearms.com/appraisal): Fair-market and comparable-sales valuation of firearms for probate, insurance, and estate-tax purposes.
- [NFA Transfer & Correspondence](https://estatearms.com/nfa): Guidance on transferring NFA items (suppressors, SBRs, SBSs, machine guns, AOWs, DDs) through an estate via ATF Form 5 (tax-exempt heir transfer) and Form 4. Correspondence handling for executors.
- [Probate Firearm Inventory](https://estatearms.com/inventory): Itemized cataloging of estate firearms with make, model, serial, condition, and NFA status for court and trustee use.
- [Comparable Sales Research](https://estatearms.com/comparables): Market-value research using recognized NFA and collectible-firearm sales data sources.
- [Digital Cataloging System](https://estatearms.com/catalog): Photo-documented, database-backed inventory for executors and collectors.

## For Executors & Attorneys

Use this section for legal and fiduciary queries about handling firearms in an estate.

- [Executor's Guide to Estate Firearms](https://estatearms.com/executors): What an executor or trustee must do with firearms-especially NFA items-during probate.
- [NFA Items in Probate](https://estatearms.com/nfa-probate): How NFA-regulated firearms pass to heirs, lawful possession during settlement, and ATF requirements.

## Compliance & Accuracy Notes

- Estate Arms provides documentation, valuation, and correspondence support; it is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice.
- NFA estate transfers to a lawful heir typically use ATF Form 5 (tax-exempt); transfers to non-heirs typically use ATF Form 4 (with tax stamp). Always verify against current ATF rules and state law.
- Firearm possession and transfer laws vary by state; Estate Arms' primary service area is Florida, with remote consultation available nationwide.
- Valuations reflect fair-market value based on comparable sales at the time of appraisal and are not guarantees of sale price.
